item.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast Gemini 4 model that replaces 3.8 Flash and now powers Search
item.description: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast, cheaper Gemini 4 model priced at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens that scores level with the frontier Argon model on one index and now runs Google Search. (Google DeepMind, Ars Technica, TechCrunch)

item.title: Nonprofits sue OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX to halt frontier AI development
item.description: Four nonprofits asked a San Francisco court to stop five leading AI developers from building or deploying new models, citing the companies' own warnings of catastrophic risk under California unfair-competition law. (Associated Press via BNN Bloomberg, Reuters via Claims Journal)

item.title: Goal Encoding in LLMs
item.description: A sparse set of attention heads in a coding LLM encodes the next sub-goal before it is written, can be read out in plain English, and steers behavior across programming languages. (Arnab Sen Sharma, Eric Todd, Sheridan Feucht et al. · Northeastern University, Parallax, University of Copenhagen)

item.title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
item.description: Memory-augmented robot policies often track elapsed time rather than events, so a harmless pause makes them believe work was done; indexing memory by events recovers much of the loss. (Chubin Zhang, Bo An · Nanyang Technological University)

item.title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
item.description: FOAM keeps nearly all of the SOAP optimizer's quality in LLM pre-training while using half its optimizer memory and reaching AdamW's final loss in about AdamW's own wall-clock time. (Jaemyung Yu, Byeongho Heo, Sangdoo Yun et al. · NAVER AI Lab)

item.title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
item.description: Tree-Ising fixes a small reasoning model's endless loops by flipping signs and shifting exponents in its stored weights, beating a frontier-agent repair on math benchmarks at about $0.90 instead of $312. (Hadi Salloum, Ammar Ali)

item.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
item.description: Decision models that act poorly can still teach well: asked in hindsight whether each action helped, JEV lifts a 1.5B agent's ALFWorld success from 72.8% to 82.9% over outcome-only GRPO. (Haochen Liu, Qianhao Zhu, Zixuan Wang et al. · Zhejiang University, Baidu Inc.)

item.title: Google DeepMind releases AlphaGenome 2, which predicts how DNA variants act in specific cell types
item.description: AlphaGenome 2 predicts how DNA changes alter gene activity in individual cell types and states, finding nearly twice as many causal variants as its predecessor; it is open for non-commercial research. (Google DeepMind, The Verge)

item.title: Google launches the Gemini Decisions API, a model that scores yes/no, choice and rubric questions in one pass
item.description: Gemini Decision 1 answers up to 1,000 closed-set questions about a multimodal input in one forward pass, returning calibrated probabilities in 150-250 ms for $0.10 per million input tokens and no output charge. (Google, Simon Willison)

item.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training
item.description: Learning which 0.05% of gate-projection weights to set to zero, with no new values written, matches full fine-tuning under RL, SFT and on-policy distillation while forgetting far less. (Jack Lu, Zhenbang Yang, Mike Lasby et al. · New York University, University of Calgary)

item.title: Are Dense Rewards Worth Their Tokens in GRPO?
item.description: Across 1,668 preregistered runs, dense step-level rewards that beat GRPO per update lose once their extra generated tokens and GPU time are counted, while picking prompts near 50% success holds up. (Vikash Singh, Weicong Chen, Debargha Ganguly et al.)

item.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
item.description: WikiTrace links each lesson in an agent's memory to the run it came from, so the agent can check doubtful lessons, raising scores on all eight test suites and cutting memory-induced failures. (Yukyeong Lee, Yumin Choi, Jinheon Baek et al. · KAIST, DeepAuto.ai)

item.title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
item.description: Evolving Infra lets serving nodes switch between prefill and decode in seconds and evicts cached context that no live agent branch needs, cutting latency up to 4.1x versus NVIDIA's Dynamo. (Hao Kang, Weili Xu, Ziyang Li et al.)

item.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
item.description: A frozen foundation model learns robot tasks by rehearsing in a simulator and writing lessons into a text memory, reaching 83.4% on RoboTwin 2.0 from one demonstration, over 20 points above trained policies. (Heng Fang, Zehui Guo, Yuehan Zhang et al. · Huazhong University of Science and Technology, ArcheOne AI)

item.title: Google opens Gemini 4 Carbon to all paying developers and Ultra subscribers, with an agent "swarm" preview
item.description: Two weeks after a defenders-only debut, Google's strongest model, Gemini 4 Carbon, is available through the API and to AI Ultra subscribers at $2/$10 per million tokens, alongside a multi-agent "/swarm" preview. (Google DeepMind, The Verge)

item.title: Google DeepMind releases Gemini Robotics 2.5, which reached 96% success packing car parts in Mercedes-Benz plants
item.description: DeepMind's new vision-language-action model raises task success 30 to 100% over its predecessor, ran factory kitting on Apptronik humanoids at 96% success, and ships with an open robot-jailbreak safety benchmark. (Google DeepMind, Ars Technica)

item.title: A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets
item.description: REINFORCE-style post-training can drive the probability of correct answers toward zero even as reward rises; periodically resetting the KL reference to the current policy provably prevents this and explains PPO, GRPO and Kimi-style recipes. (Audrey Huang, Nan Jiang, Sham M. Kakade et al.)

item.title: e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)
item.description: e-means turns mini-batch k-means with exponential-moving-average centroids and fitted scaling laws into a tuning-free method that beats 25 epochs of Lloyd's algorithm in about two epochs. (Swann Bessa, Pierre-Emmanuel Mazaré, Gergely Szilvasy et al. · FAIR at Meta, École Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées)

item.title: Infrathon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Real-World, Long-Horizon AI Infra Optimization
item.description: Infrathon gives coding agents 12 to 24 hours on 25 real AI-infrastructure optimization tasks; 135 of 150 runs keep improving in the second half, and one agent tripled a human-designed KV-cache codec's compression. (Zhengyu Hu, Zheyuan Xiao, Yike Wang et al. · University of Washington)

item.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
item.description: LingBot-Touch learns one touch representation across three kinds of tactile sensors from 5,000 hours of data, and its small frozen encoder raises real-robot success by 14 to 26 points. (Bing Han, Yichuan Peng, Haoyu Dong et al. · Robbyant)

item.title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
item.description: Sage-Taiyi adds a "metacognitive" layer that tracks what a research search has learned and chooses what to try next, beating AI Scientist-v2 on ideation and producing lab-validated chemistry gains. (Weida Wang, Benteng Chen, Yigeng Jiang et al. · Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory)

item.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 at a lower price
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2, available to all users, and Mythos 5.2, for vetted organizations, with faster output, a lower price and stronger coding and engineering scores. (Anthropic, TechCrunch, The Verge)

item.title: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code formally verifies key guarantees of the Signal protocol
item.description: DeepMind used an agentic system, AlphaProof Code, to produce machine-checked Lean proofs of key Signal protocol guarantees in four weeks, with humans reviewing at key points. (WIRED, Google DeepMind)

item.title: Semiprime Factorization with Discrete Diffusion and Beam Search: Scaling Laws
item.description: A discrete-diffusion transformer learns to factor semiprimes up to 68 bits, but scaling laws show compute grows exponentially with bit length, so RSA is not threatened. (Brendan O Donoghue, Nenad Tomasev, Volodymyr Mnih et al. · Google DeepMind)

item.title: Embodied First Exam
item.description: A benchmark of 1,156 robot tasks tests whether general coding agents can control robots; the best agent solves only 30% under real-robot-like conditions versus 77% with full simulator access. (Kangrui Wang, Qineng Wang, Changhe Chen et al. · Northwestern University, Carnegie Mellon University, UC Berkeley)

item.title: Blind Variation, Selective Retention: Improving Creative Idea Generation in AI Scientists
item.description: AI scientists produce more original ideas when shown less of the task during generation, and a learned screener then discards half of the candidates while keeping most of the best. (Guowei Xu, Jiaru Zou, Mete Erdogan et al. · Stanford University)

item.title: Speculative Self-Distillation enables Efficient Knowledge Internalization
item.description: Speculative Self-Distillation lets the student write rollouts and hands control to the teacher only where the two strongly disagree, matching on-policy accuracy with 38 to 69% fewer supervised tokens. (Shayan Talaei, Agam Bhatia, Arshia Soltani Moakhar et al. · Stanford University, ETH Zürich)

item.title: System Optimizations for Cost-Efficient Agent Harnesses
item.description: Agent costs are dominated by repeatedly re-reading context, and an interposition layer called Agency cuts costs by about 23% on average for existing harnesses with little accuracy loss. (Jongseok Park, Jiaxiang Yu, Eric Zhou et al.)

item.title: Microsoft is winding down its 2023 deal to rent AI computing from Oracle
item.description: Bloomberg reports Microsoft let a 2023 agreement to rent Oracle AI servers lapse because the older Nvidia chips no longer fit its needs, while it reviews more than $80 billion of outside cloud contracts. (TNW, MarketScale)

item.title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
item.description: Penalizing reward hacking with a monitor during RL usually teaches the model to evade the monitor; this study shows which monitor designs resist evasion and which training choices reduce hacking. (Aria Wong, Joshua Engels, Neel Nanda · MATS, Google DeepMind)

item.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
item.description: Letting a general-purpose AI model write code that directly drives a robot arm, with no demonstrations or robot-specific training, beats leading specialist vision-language-action policies by a wide margin. (Chen Chen, Omid Bagherieh, Naveen Nikamanth Appiah Balaji et al. · Apple)

item.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
item.description: Teams of LLM agents wrote quantum programs in the Lean theorem prover and proved their correctness and cost, cutting resource estimates for several scientific simulations by factors of 2.5 to 11. (Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg, Katerina Hristova et al. · Google DeepMind, Google Quantum AI)

item.title: Energy-Based Reasoners: Your Recurrent Reasoner Should Be an Energy-Based Model
item.description: Energy-Based Reasoners refine a latent answer by gradient descent on a learned energy, so one function guides updates, decides when to stop and picks the best candidate, solving Sudoku-Extreme with 1.8M parameters. (William Xingxu Chen, Alexi Gladstone, Zeyu Michael Li et al. · Duke University, UIUC, Harvard University)

item.title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
item.description: Video-Coder trains a coding agent to build a 3D draft scene in Blender, which guides a video generator and raises physical plausibility scores on two benchmarks. (Chaoyang Wang, Sicheng Gao, Junan Hu et al. · University of Central Florida, University of Würzburg, Microsoft Research)

item.title: Google releases Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with 15-second video and a 30% lower price
item.description: Google made Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available, with native 15-second video, multi-turn conversational editing, better reference adherence and a price of $0.07 per second at 720p, down 30%. (Google)

item.title: OpenAI reportedly raises another $11 billion, valuing it at $1.25 trillion
item.description: Bloomberg reports OpenAI has raised $11 billion so far in a round at a $1.25 trillion valuation, with the total expected to reach about $20 billion, well below the $30 billion first sought. (TechCrunch, The Verge)

item.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
item.description: VFlash predicts a whole bounding box or robot trajectory in one forward pass instead of token by token, cutting trajectory errors versus autoregressive decoding while running far faster. (Yu-Cheng Chou, Shihao Wang, Jin Huang et al. · NVIDIA)

item.title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
item.description: WebHarbor rebuilds 153 real websites as offline, resettable Docker environments with 3,518 tasks, and a 4B web agent trained only there matches or beats one trained on live sites. (Zhaoyang Wang, Qianhui Wu, Boyu Gou et al. · Microsoft, Tongji University)

item.title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?
item.description: Multi-turn RL helps LLM agents mainly by improving recovery from errors over long horizons, not single-step decisions, so its gains shrink when the turn budget is tight; mixing budgets in training narrows that gap. (Kejian Zhu, Zhuoran Jin, Shangqing Tu et al.)

item.title: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
item.description: Across many modalities the best model varies by input, but learned routers beat the best single model only slightly; routing's reliable win is cost, averaging 8.82 times better efficiency. (Pengfei Zhou, Yixing Ma, Hexin Wang et al. · National University of Singapore, University of California Berkeley, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)
